entries.claim: A confounder is a variable that affects both the treatment and the outcome, so an observed association can be spurious; larger samples reduce random error but not confounding bias
entries.notes: Bias does not vanish as n grows

entries.claim: Observational studies suggested hormone replacement therapy reduced coronary risk, but the randomised Women's Health Initiative trial found increased coronary heart disease, stroke and breast cancer risks
The backdoor criterion identifies a set of variables that, when conditioned on, block all non-causal paths from treatment to outcome so the remaining association can be interpreted causally
entries.locator: Hernán & Robins, Causal Inference: What If, Chapter 6-7
entries.notes: Assumes the causal diagram is correct

entries.claim: Pearl's ladder distinguishes association, intervention P(Y|do(X)), and counterfactuals, with each higher rung requiring more causal assumptions
Random assignment makes treatment groups comparable in expectation, blocking arrows into the treatment and removing confounding; intention-to-treat preserves this when adherence is imperfect
entries.locator: Hernán & Robins, Causal Inference: What If, randomised experiments
entries.notes: Comes with ethical, cost and external-validity limits

entries.claim: In the teaching model X = Z + noise, Y = 3000*X + c*Z + noise, the naive slope is about 3000 + c/2 while the adjusted slope is 3000
entries.notes: Exact under the stated linear model with a = 1
